description: We are TechStars, a team of three passionate girls with interests in AI/ML, space exploration, data analysis, and technology-driven innovation. We enjoy solving real-world challenges through creative thinking, research, and technical skills.
summary:
The project transforms NASA planetary observations into synchronized, interactive acoustic compositions. Each scientific dataset—from Black Marble nocturnal radiance to GEDI forest lidar and ocean salinity—acts as a playable "vinyl record." As a virtual turntable needle sweeps temporally across the data, our dual Python and browser-based Web Audio engine translates physical parameters into music: horizontal coordinates dictate stereo panning, latitude determines pitch quantized to musical scales, luminance drives velocity, and motion governs rhythmic density.

Beyond pre-rendered archival audio, we developed "Bring Your Own Earth", an in-browser sonification pipeline that ingests any user-uploaded Earth observation video, extracts multi-strip features in real time, and synthesizes dynamic audio with four custom instrument presets

TerraTone addresses the challenge of making complex, multidimensional remote sensing datasets intuitive and universally accessible. By pairing precise spectrogram visualization with harmonized auditory feedback, it unlocks planetary science for visually impaired researchers and broad audiences alike—turning abstract scientific telemetry into an immersive sensory journey through Earth’s changing systems.
details:
1. What does it do, and how does it work?

It sonifies NASA Earth observation datasets by treating planetary visualizations as interactive "vinyl records." A glowing turntable needle sweeps left to right across time, translating visual and sensor data directly into musical soundscapes.

The system operates via a synchronized two-part architecture:

The Mathematical Sonification Mapping Engine:

Horizontal Axis (X / Time): Governs temporal progression and dynamic binaural stereo panning (-1.0 left to +1.0 right) across 32 distinct spatial strips.

Vertical Axis (Y / Latitude / Strip Height): Drives musical pitch. Vertical strip positions are mapped and quantized to harmonically stable musical scales (such as A-minor and C-major pentatonic, blues, or diatonic scales) across multiple octaves.

Luminance / Brightness: Controls note velocity, amplitude gain (via perceptual square-root scaling), and filter cutoffs.

Dominant Hue: Determines instrument timbre and harmonic family (e.g., warm hues evoke strings and bells; cool hues trigger resonant pads).

Inter-frame Motion: Modulates note duration, envelope attack/release times, rhythmic density, and LFO vibrato depth.

Dual-Track Dual-Epoch Comparison ("Then vs. Now"):

Displays stacked timelines comparing historical baselines (e.g., 2012 Night Lights) against recent observations (2023). Stable areas produce consonant foundations, growth generates harmonizing chords, and environmental decline introduces tension and dissonance.

"Bring Your Own Earth" (Live Client-Side Sonification):

Users can upload any custom Earth observation video (MP4/WebM). An in-browser computer vision pipeline dynamically samples frames at 640×360, computes 32-strip luminance and motion vectors, and drives real-time audio synthesis via the Web Audio API with an overlay oscilloscope visualizer.

2. What benefits does it have?

Accessible Science (Universal Design): Opens complex remote sensing data to blind and low-vision researchers, educators, and students who traditionally face steep visual barriers.

Multimodal Pattern Recognition: The human auditory cortex is uniquely adept at detecting minute rhythmic shifts, frequency changes, and subtle anomalies that might be overlooked in visual heatmaps or satellite imagery alone.

Immediate Public Engagement: Eliminates technical GIS barriers. Anyone can interactively scrub, play, probe, and listen to planetary changes without specialist software.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Educational Outreach: Transforming abstract climate datasets (deforestation, ocean warming, urbanization, atmospheric lightning) into memorable emotional and acoustic experiences for classrooms, science centers, and planetariums.

Planetary Awareness: Providing an intuitive, visceral way to experience climate change—allowing listeners to literally hear planetary growth, seasonal pulses, and ecological loss over decades.

Inclusive Data Exploration: Establishing a reproducible standard for scientific data sonification that can be adopted across other NASA science missions (e.g., planetary exploration, astrophysics, heliophysics).

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used?

Languages & Core Technologies:

JavaScript (ES6+ Module Architecture): Powers the client-side UI, video frame extraction, and real-time audio synthesis without external dependencies.

Python 3: Powers the high-fidelity offline audio rendering pipeline and validation suites.

HTML5 & CSS3: Hardware-accelerated UI with custom HUD aesthetics, SVG icons, and responsive canvas rendering.

APIs & Libraries:

Web Audio API: Nodes including AudioContext, StereoPannerNode, DynamicsCompressorNode, BiquadFilterNode, AnalyserNode, and polyphonic OscillatorNode setups.

Canvas API & OffscreenCanvas: Used for high-speed video downscaling, frame extraction, spectrogram rendering, and live audio oscilloscope visualizers.

NumPy & SciPy (Python): Digital signal processing, buffer management, ADSR envelopes, scale quantization, and audio mixing.

FluidSynth & SoundFonts (Python): Optional MIDI-based acoustic instrument rendering.

FFmpeg / ffprobe & OpenCV: Video duration verification, frame extraction, and metadata alignment.

5. How is your project creative?

The "Planetary Vinyl" Metaphor: Blending retro analog jukebox nostalgia with precision scientific instrumentation bridges the gap between art and astrophysics.

Interactive Coordinate Probe ("Touch the Earth"): Users can hover, touch, or navigate with keyboard arrows across any coordinate on the visualizer to audit the localized musical frequency, luminance magnitude, and spectral category of specific geographic strips.

Dynamic Acoustic Presets: Four custom instrument synthesis profiles let users experience the data through different timbres:

a. Synth Pad: Warm ambient dual-oscillator pad with brightness-controlled low-pass filters.

b. Mallet: Bell/marimba strike with non-harmonic overtones (2.76× and 5.4×), ideal for point-source nighttime lights.

c. Strings: Chorus-detuned sawtooth oscillators with motion-modulated vibrato.

d. Lab Sine: Transparent pure sine tones tailored for scientific sonification audits.

6. What factors did your team consider?

Autoplay & Audio Graph Safety: Browser security policies mandate that audio graphs start on user gestures. We architected a shared, idempotent audio graph (voice nodes → instrumentGain → masterAnalyser → masterGain → compressor → destination) that handles suspended states gracefully without memory leaks.

Acoustic Fatigue & Musicality: Raw data can easily sound harsh or chaotic. We implemented voice capping (maximum 4 concurrent voices), brightness noise-gating thresholds (skipping strips below 0.15 brightness), exponential ADSR envelopes to eliminate digital clicks, and soft-knee peak compression.

Data Integrity Over Fabrication: All sound directly maps to measured physical quantities. We strictly avoided synthetic or placeholder data, building robust self-check test suites that verify note duration, scale membership, and positive pitch-to-height correlation against real NASA telemetry files.

Accessibility (WCAG Compliance): Full keyboard navigation (Space, Arrow keys, Mute, Probe shortcuts), ARIA live region announcements for preset changes, and high-contrast HUD layouts.
